governance.attested_by: nyiso-89 session 2026-07-27: the nyiso-87 keeper recipe re-solved across 2023-2025 on current main with ONE delta, not fitted to any residual — measured_ct_heat_rates=True. CT_PEAKER generators at the 19 plants the committed CAMPD artifact covers take their plant's MEASURED LOADED heat rate (MMBtu per NET MWh) ahead of the eGRID PLANT-AVERAGE ANNUAL rate. The eGRID figure is defective for a peaker twice over: an annual average blends start / part-load / shutdown fuel into the number that sets an offer, and eGRID publishes ONE rate per plant, so at a mixed facility the turbines inherit the steam boilers' rate. Applied per generator BY CLASS, so only a mixed plant's turbines are repriced. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] promotion: this run is the more structurally faithful of the pair, NOT the better-fitting one — see _open_items (2). Scored against its own same-HEAD zero-delta control (2026-07-27-nyiso-89-control-zerodelta), never against registered keeper metrics.
governance.note: Rule 13 [R-MEASURED] admissibility of the new mechanism: every input is either the model's OWN P0 solution (run pattern, duals) or a forward-derivable physical constant, so nothing is pinned to a NYISO outcome and the whole mechanism regenerates for a forecast year and responds to changed conditions. The two min_load_frac values and two min_run_hours are measured unit CONDUCT (CAMPD 2023-2025), the class of input rule 13 explicitly admits; they were never swept, and the reconstructed CC min-load 0.523 is corroborated OUT OF SAMPLE by ERCOT's independently published 0.574. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE] is satisfied by construction: the NYISO values live in NYISO-only fields and the ERCOT bridge's 0.574 was NOT transplanted - the agreement is a check, not a source. ARM D CONTRAST, recorded because it is the rule-1 case in its purest form: a probe arming td_loss_factor=0.0251 flips the same C1 cell AND improves C3c more than any arm here (2025 tail 9h -> 18h), but breaks C5a (2025 CO2 +8.1 -> +14.2 %, out of band). If that extra 3.7 TWh were real load the fleet serves, burning it would not push measured-plant-rate CO2 four points past its band - independent physical corroboration of docs/nyiso-td-loss-resolution-2026-06.md, whose Gold Book Table I-2 Note 1 already established that the served demand is loss-INCLUSIVE. The better-fitting arm is the wrong answer, and this keeper deliberately does not use it.
governance.residuals_note: SCORED EFFECT vs the de-designated nyiso-81 keeper. C1 fuel-mix - NYISO's load-bearing FAIL - CLOSES: the 2023 CC_REGULAR cell walks -4.11 (same-HEAD control) -> -3.32 (limbs off) -> -3.20 (+physical bar) -> -2.89 (+econ+min-run at class tables) -> -2.78 TWh here, against a +/-2.94 band. It closes with td_loss_factor still 0.0, which is the OPPOSITE of what nyiso-86 sec 2.1 expected: that section nominated td_loss_factor as C1's instrument, and the cell closed instead by re-timing gas the model was already free to dispatch. The margin is thin (~0.16 of +/-2.94 TWh) and is recorded as such. Also improved: C3a 2024/2025 -5.5/-6.7 % -> -3.2/-4.7 %, C5a 2025 +8.1 -> +7.6 %, C8 2024 ST_GAS forced share 36.2 -> 31.9 % (still grounded above budget), and the ungated nyiso-86 sec 3 interchange defect moves monotonically toward the measurement from BOTH ends (imports hod01-03 3,048 -> 2,797 vs actual 2,596; hod16-18 2,381 -> 2,713 vs 2,857; within-month r +0.072 -> +0.108) under a mechanism that touches no seam wiring. D-2 shows SUBSTITUTION WITH LESS TOTAL FORCING: 2023 merchant-gas forced energy 4.46 -> 4.18 TWh, with reliability_floor giving up CT_PEAKER entirely plus part of ST_GAS and the bridge id picking up CC_REGULAR. DEGRADED, recorded and deliberately NOT reverted per rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: C3c 2025 falls 9h -> 6h against a 42h actual. More online capacity at the peak means more headroom under the $258 mainland roof; C3c is roof-blocked (nyiso-85 sec 7d), not tightness-blocked, and a structurally-correct commitment mechanism stays in even when a residual moves the wrong way. C3c is now the SOLE blocking criterion (it was C1 + C3c). CT_PEAKER volume collapses 1.42 -> 0.46 TWh against a 2.26 actual once its only floor is removed - reported honestly, not patched with a re-armed floor; its SHAPE improved in every year while its level fell, which is the point.

_open_items: (0) nyiso-89 CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE, recorded because it changes what this class's residual means: nyiso-88 §4 compared a CAMPD GROSS-basis loaded heat rate against the model's NET-basis eGRID rate. CAMPD meters gross load while eGRID, the LP's dispatched MW and the benchmark's own actual (gross x parasitic_factor) are all net. On a common net basis the generation-weighted SRMC bias is +$1.37/+$1.49/+$2.50 per MWh, NOT the published +$6.48/+$6.70/+$7.34; capacity-weighted the model UNDERCHARGES the class by $0.91-$1.66/MWh. nyiso-88's headline — that the cost error exceeds the margin the fleet earns in every year — does not survive against the measured margin -$1.39/+$5.82/+$3.49. | (1) CT_PEAKER's LEVEL REMAINS THE DOMINANT OPEN ITEM and this bundle does NOT close it: 0.443/0.394/1.407 TWh against 2.260/2.134/3.011 actual. The measured heat rate moves it -0.016/+0.080/+0.125 TWh = -0.9 %/+4.4 %/+7.2 % of the gap, with 2023 moving the WRONG WAY (correcting Barrett upward removes more capacity from merit than Bayswater and the in-city fleet add back). THE HEAT RATE IS NOW ELIMINATED AS THIS CLASS'S CANDIDATE rather than confirmed as one. Day-ahead BLOCK COMMITMENT is what remains, to be judged against the measured CT run-length distribution (median 4 h, mean 6.5-7.6 h, p90 14 h) rather than against the volume gap. It must NOT be closed by re-arming a windowed floor — the mechanism the owner rejected 2026-07-27. | (2) PROMOTED ON STRUCTURE, NOT FIT (rule 1): every criterion verdict is IDENTICAL to the control. C1 PASS 14/14 both, but the thin cell moves marginally the WRONG way — 2023 CC_REGULAR -2.775 -> -2.784 TWh against ±2.94, margin 0.165 -> 0.156 TWh. C5a 2025 +7.57 % -> +7.62 % (CO2 measured, not assumed: the two effects do not cancel and the net is slightly positive, because the energy CT_PEAKER gains comes from ST_GAS/CC_REGULAR, which burn at lower heat rates than a peaker). C3c 2025 6 -> 7 h vs 42, still FAIL and still the sole blocking criterion. This is an accuracy swap kept under rule 14 even though the residual did not improve. | (3) LOYO caveat on the derived input — see the measured_ct_heat_rates ledger entry's root_cause: stable for 16 of 19 plants, NOT stable on the two thin-sampled barge plants (Gowanus, Narrows), which sit far out of merit at every fold value so no gate moves. A minimum-energy screen is the named follow-up, deliberately not added post-hoc. | (4) 23 plants (219 MW) carry no measured rate and keep their eGRID value — the correct fallback, never a hand number. | (5) INHERITED from nyiso-87 and NOT addressed here: the nyiso-88 §5 benchmark multi-class collapse (render_calibration_html.py keys mw_p by plant_code while iterating (plant_code, klass), so a plant spanning two model classes is attributed whole to its alphabetically-last class). Worth only -0.24 TWh on CT_PEAKER but ±2.1-2.5 TWh on ST_GAS/ST_CHP/CC_*; cross-ISO (NYISO 13.9 %, MISO 9.2 %, ERCOT 8.8 %). Needs its own owner-scoped lane.

entries.name: nyiso_gas_commitment_bridge (min_load_frac + min_run_hours)
entries.source: ALL FOUR values read from ONE frozen derive artifact, data/raw/_processed-legacy/campd_gas_commitment_params_NYISO.csv (scripts/data/derive_campd_gas_commitment_params.py, EPA CAMPD unit-level hourly grossLoad 2023-2025, 78 units). min_load_frac = the capacity-weighted p50 across units of each unit's own LSL/HSL ratio, where HSL = p99.5 of pooled load and LSL = p5 of online-hour load (the WP-3 loading-when-on construction + the derive_cc_committed_pct.py p5-of-online minimum-stable statistic). min_run_hours = the capacity-weighted p50 of the measured run-length distribution (CC p25/p50/p75 = 11/21/133 h; ST_GAS 3/13/89 h). NYISO publishes no 60-Day-DAM equivalent of the ERCOT LSL/HSL disclosure, which is why the ratio is reconstructed from the meter; the reconstructed CC value 0.523 lands within 9 % of ERCOT's independently PUBLISHED cap-weighted p50 of 0.574 — an outside cross-check that the construction is not self-referential.
entries.note: ZERO residual identification: no value was chosen for its effect on a price or volume residual, and none was swept. The capacity weighting is forced by what the parameter does (a min-run constraint floors committed MW, not committed unit-count) and is the same weighting min_load_frac uses. The min-run values DISAGREE with the published class tables in OPPOSITE directions — CC 21 h is an increase over the table's 5-10 h, ST_GAS 13 h a decrease from its 24-48 h — which is itself evidence the values follow the measurement rather than a residual: a residual-fitted pair would not move against a published table in one class and with it in the other. Caveat recorded: an OBSERVED run length is an upper-ish bound on a minimum-run CONSTRAINT, so the low percentiles bound it from the side the constraint lives on; the p50 is the deliberate, documented choice and re-derives ONLY when the CAMPD vintages update (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]). The mechanism's other inputs add no parameters at all: min-down and startup cost come from the published NREL/SR-5500-55433 class tables the model already used, the DA horizon is the tariff-cited DA_COMMITMENT_HORIZON_HOURS=24, and the restart inequality is priced at the model's OWN P0 duals. n_residual UNCHANGED at 6.

construction.window: grossLoad >= 0.80 x p95 of that unit's own gross load
construction.gross_to_net: divided by the COMMITTED parasitic factor (parasitic_load_factors.parquet) -- the same map run_calibration_full._campd_hourly_frame uses to build the benchmark's net actual
construction.plant_aggregation: generation-weighted mean over the plant's turbines

entries.source: EPA CAMPD unit-level hourly grossLoad + heatInput. Replaces the eGRID PLANT-AVERAGE ANNUAL heat rate, which is neither a loaded rate nor -- at a mixed facility -- the right technology's rate (E F Barrett 2511: 1971 FT4 turbines and 188 MW steam boilers share one 11.076; measured separately the turbines run 16.69. Bayswater 55699 carries a non-physical 21.68 against a measured 10.74).
entries.identification_note: ZERO fitted scalars. Every value is a measured unit-conduct statistic; no parameter of the construction (window, percentile, minimum hours, band) was chosen by looking at a residual. Rule 13 [R-MEASURED] admissible: a machine's loaded heat rate regenerates for a forward year from the same pipeline and responds to changed conditions (a retrofit moves it; a new unit carries its design rate). Rule 24 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]: re-derives ONLY on a CAMPD vintage change.
entries.root_cause: OPEN (LOYO caveat, nyiso-89): re-deriving the artifact leaving each year out is stable for 16 of 19 plants (<5 % spread) and never reverses the correction's sign on any plant that carries its weight -- Bayonne 0.5 %, Bayswater 1.0 %, Port Jefferson 2.8 %, Barrett 6.1 % (16.07-17.09, never approaching the eGRID 11.08). It is NOT stable on the two low-utilization 1970s barge plants: Gowanus 2494 (16.5 % spread) and Narrows 2499 (12.8 %), where dropping 2025 reverses the sign vs eGRID. Those plants are thin-sampled (0.09 and 0.22 TWh of measured energy across three years) and sit far out of merit at EVERY fold value (13.2-16.2 MMBtu/MWh against a class base near 10), so no gate moves. A minimum-energy screen for thin-sampled plants is the named follow-up; it is deliberately NOT added here, because adding a screen after seeing the LOYO result would be a post-hoc choice (rule 24).
